clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move across the country in March 1952, within a year: June's homesickness and anxiety rose, she wrote daily to her sister Edna; Walter kept to the trees and distanced from June; Glen fought at school and was sent home twice; Walter stopped writing to his brother Harlan after a quarrel over their father's land money; June's functioning fell and she kept to her bed for weeks that first winter; Walter and June had rows over money for new trees; by September 1953, June joined the church choir and her anxiety eased as her functioning rose and her letters to Edna thinned out. These shifts belong together as the family's reactions to the move and the orchard's early struggles.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when a late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan, within a year: Walter drank heavily most nights; Walter and Glen blamed each other in loud conflict over the loan; Glen and Marian overfunctioned, taking over the family's money and talks with the bank; Carl's asthma attacks worsened that winter; Ida's heart trouble was found and she was told to stop working at the bakery; by spring 1969 Carl's asthma eased, but Nora began wetting the bed in April; by October 1969 Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees, his functioning rose. The sale of the orchard in October 1968 sits within these months.

clusters.name: Glen's job loss at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's loss of his job in February 1975 when the Ridgeport cannery closed, within a year: Glen's functioning fell, he sat in the truck in the yard for hours most of that year; Glen and Marian fought loud rows at night over money; Marian overfunctioned, taking a second job cleaning offices at night; Nora stopped eating properly and lost a lot of weight that summer; Nora distanced from Marian, kept to her room and said little; Walter drank again after six years off it in December; by March 1976 Glen started driving a delivery truck for the feed store; by June 1976 Nora's functioning rose, she ate again and made the track team. Nora's own troubles stand at the centre of these months, and no one else's shifts show then.

clusters.name: Wilma's move into Nora's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma's move into Nora and Hollis's house in January 1990, within a year and a half: Nora and Wilma clashed over the children's bedtimes and meals; Hollis worked late and distanced from Nora over the kitchen rows; Hollis moved toward his mother's side; Owen had tantrums at preschool and was sent home twice; Wilma overfunctioned, taking over Lily's care; Nora's eczema flared on both hands; Nora and Hollis had rows most nights; Nora's anxiety rose and she phoned her mother twice a week; in June 1991 Wilma took a flat in town; by August 1991 Nora's eczema cleared over the summer and her functioning rose. The shifts pass from one person to the next around Wilma's arrival and her departure.

periods.name: the year Dad lost his job
periods.words: The one that stands out is the year Dad lost his job, when I was 14.

declined.reason: 1994: an acute episode. The wildfire on August 12–16, 1994 brought several shifts—Nora's anxiety rose, Lily was sick to her stomach, Owen would not sleep without a light on, Nora and Hollis clashed over driving out—all within the same few days around a real threat. By August 16 they were allowed home and calm returned within the week, with the children back at school. This is a reaction to a real event that settled within days, not a period.

1996–1997: not enough in the diagram to choose a reading. The recount leaves two shifts that count: Tess's drinking rose in October 1996 and Nora's anxiety rose in November 1996 when she phoned Tess every night, worried for her; Marian overfunctioned with Tess, but this shift is marked neverOpens; Tess and Rick had shouting matches in March 1997 and Tess stopped drinking in June 1997. No change in the family on a known date sits among these events—Tess's troubles are her own, and no event says a structural change opened this time in Nora's family.
